title: Probability of Compound Events
short: Find a compound probability as a fraction of the sample space.
trouble: Students add the probabilities of two independent events when they should multiply them.

blocks.html: A compound event is made of two or more simple events, like "heads and a 6." With a sample space you can find its probability by counting, and multiplying fractions gives a shortcut.

For equally likely outcomes, $$P(\text{event}) = \frac{\text{favorable outcomes}}{\text{all outcomes in the sample space}}$$ When the events do not affect each other (independent events), $P(A \text{ and } B) = P(A) \times P(B)$.

Half of all coin flips are heads, and $\frac{1}{6}$ of those also come with a 6 on the number cube. A fraction of a fraction is a product: $\frac{1}{6}$ of $\frac{1}{2}$ is $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}$. The tree shows the same thing: multiply along a path.

blocks.name: tree
blocks.cap: Three coins: 8 equally likely paths, each with probability $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{8}$. Select outcomes to build an event.

blocks.title: Coin and number cube
blocks.q: A coin is flipped and a number cube is rolled. Find the probability of heads and a 6.
steps: Sample space: $2 \times 6 = 12$ equally likely outcomes. Only H6 fits.

blocks.title: At least one head
blocks.q: Three coins are flipped. Find the probability of at least one head.
steps: Of the 8 outcomes, only TTT has no head.

blocks.title: Two number cubes
blocks.q: Find the probability that two number cubes have a sum of 8.

blocks.html: Adding instead of multiplying for "and": $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$ for heads and a 6. That is bigger than either chance alone, but needing both things to happen must be less likely than needing one. Check: is your answer smaller than each single probability?
